scraped.scraped_description: SecureDrop is an open-source whistleblower submission system that media organizations can install to securely accept documents from anonymous sources. It was originally coded by the late Aaron Swartz and is now managed by Freedom of the Press Foundation.

name: SecureDrop
tagline: Open source whistleblower submission system for secure anonymous document sharing
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
awards: Freedom of the Press Foundation recognition
policy_outcomes: Adoption by major news organizations for source protection
Influence on media industry standards for whistleblower protection
documented_limitations: Requires users to understand Tor Browser and anonymity practices
Dependent on individual organizations to maintain secure installations
No IP logging means limited ability to detect abuse
failure_modes: User failure to properly use Tor Browser
curation_criteria: Open source contribution guidelines; code review process managed by Freedom of the Press Foundation
contributor_governance: Merit-based; contributions reviewed by core team
controversies: Debate over effectiveness of anonymity protections
legal_regulatory_issues: Potential legal challenges in authoritarian jurisdictions; legal support provided by Freedom of the Press Foundation
political_relevance_summary: Addresses government transparency and press freedom by providing a secure, anonymous whistleblower submission system used by major news organizations worldwide.

movement_building_utility.notes: Provides technical infrastructure supporting civic technology ecosystem.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication; already deployed across multiple jurisdictions; replication materials are available.
